x-uikit.intent: Show one or more sections at a time, collapsing the rest to their headers.
typical_uses: A list of independent sections (FAQ, settings groups) too long to show all at once, where the user opens what is relevant
Progressive disclosure of grouped content under named headers

invariants.text: With `multiple` at its default of false, opening one item closes any other open item - at most one item is open at a time.

Every `AccordionItem`'s `value` must be unique within THIS root - not across roots. Base UI's Accordion.Root keeps its own value state and its own keyboard-navigation list, each scoped to that root's React context; a nested `Accordion` inside another's panel resolves its OWN root context, so its items may safely reuse a value already used by an ancestor root without any collision.

anti_patterns.dont: Put an always-visible required form control inside a collapsed panel
anti_patterns.instead: Keep required fields outside the accordion, or default that item's panel open - a screen reader user tabbing through the page will not discover a hidden required field until they expand that section

anti_patterns.dont: Reuse the same `value` for two items inside the SAME accordion root
anti_patterns.instead: Give every item a unique `value` within its own root - a nested `Accordion` needs no coordination with its ancestor's values, only with its own siblings

good.title: Two sections, single-expansion (the default)
good.code:
<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem value="item-1">
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it accessible?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Yes. It adheres to the WAI-ARIA design pattern.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="item-2">
    <AccordionTrigger>Is it styled?</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Yes, with the kit's own tokens.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

bad.title: A single section used as a show/hide toggle
bad.why: One section is not what an accordion is for - it carries Base UI's multi-item expansion machinery for nothing to coordinate. Reach for `Collapsible` instead.

dont_use_when.rule: A single show/hide toggle for one piece of content
Primary navigation between sections that stays visible

assumptions.claim: value is an array of the root's own generic Value parameter
assumptions.reason: `AccordionValue<Value>` is an ARRAY of the type parameter, not a single value, and a generic has no JSON Schema representation - which is exactly the misreading this entry exists to prevent: an agent shown an unconstrained `value` concluded it took a plain string. The property carries the checker's own printed type text. accordion.md's example uses string item values (`value="item-1"` on the item), so a root value is an array of those.

assumptions.claim: defaultValue is an array of the root's own generic Value parameter
assumptions.reason: Same type as `value` above, and the same reason nothing asserts it - the uncontrolled starting point is a LIST of open item values, not one of them.

assumptions.claim: onValueChange is a callback, not a value
assumptions.reason: `(value: AccordionValue<Value>, eventDetails) => void` - a function of the generic above plus Base UI's own event-details object. No JSON Schema type covers a function.

assumptions.claim: render replaces the root element with one the caller supplies
assumptions.reason: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the root's state; neither is expressible in JSON Schema. Replacing the root element means taking over the wrapper the kit's own layout styles (`.root`) are attached to.

assumptions.claim: style accepts a function of the root's state as well as a plain style object
assumptions.reason: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)`; a JSON Schema `object` would reject the function form.

hidden.reason: The root's own stylesheet fixes the layout to a single column (accordion.module.css's `.root { flex-direction: column }`), so the only value `orientation` could add - "horizontal" - would put Base UI's horizontal keyboard axis on a vertical layout. Hidden rather than listed: a contract listing it would be this kit's own statement that it works.
